reason: MessageDigest ENSURES digested[out, _] and digested[out, inbytearr] in both anchors, and no rule in either REQUIRES digested. The predicate is terminal: that a byte array is a digest is stated and never consulted, so a reader would have to be invented rather than transcribed.

KeyPairGenerator ENSURES generatedKeypair[kp, alg] and KeyPair ENSURES generatedKeypair[this, _] after co; no rule in either anchor REQUIRES the predicate. What the downstream rules ask for are the pair's halves, generatedPrivkey and generatedPubkey, carried by GENERATED_PRIVATE_KEY and GENERATED_PUBLIC_KEY -- both of which are read.

Holds the first place of macced[M, D] -- M is the MAC of D. The predicate's only consumer is the Cipher rule's !macced[_, plainText], which leaves that place anonymous, so the read projects onto the second place alone: MACED carries it and CipherSpec reads it (D-S13). The first place has no reader because of the shape of the clause, not because one was omitted.

The API 30 TrustManagerFactory rule ensures generatedTrustManager of two different objects -- the factory itself after Init, and the array returned by getTrustManagers -- and the set carries the two places in two constants. SSLContext requires only the array, so GENERATED_TRUST_MANAGERS is the one SSLContextSpec reads. No rule in either anchor requires the factory itself.

SSLContext ENSURES generatedSSLContext[this] after Init in both anchors and no rule REQUIRES it. The context is the end of this chain: nothing in either corpus consumes a configured SSLContext, so the predicate is terminal.

SSLContext ENSURES generatedSSLEngine[eng] in both anchors, and CrySL 1.5.2 also has the SSLEngine rule ensure it of itself. No rule in either anchor REQUIRES it -- terminal, like generatedSSLContext.

PBEParameterSpec ENSURES preparedPBE[this] in both anchors. Its only consumer is the AlgorithmParameters rule of CrySL 1.5.2 -- the API 30 derivation drops that REQUIRES -- and AlgorithmParameters has no .mop in this set of 23. The reader is absent because the consuming rule is unmodelled here, which is D-S14's criterion seen from the producing side.
Signature ENSURES signed[out, ...] after Signs in both anchors, once per input overload, and no rule REQUIRES signed. Terminal: nothing in either corpus consumes a signature.

PBEKeySpec and SecretKeySpec ENSURE speccedKey in both anchors and this set models both producers. The consumers are SecretKeyFactory (both anchors) and KeyFactory (1.5.2), neither of which has a .mop here, so the read cannot be transcribed without first adding the specification that would perform it (D-S14).
Signature ENSURES verified[sign] (API 30) and verified[verified, sign] after Verifies (1.5.2), and no rule in either anchor REQUIRES it. Terminal, like signed.

Cipher.crysl ENSURES wrappedKey[wrappedKeyBytes, wrappedKey] and no rule in either anchor REQUIRES it; the API 30 derivation drops the ENSURES as well. The write transcribes a clause with no consumer on either side of the anchor.
